# Achieve Life Sciences Becomes AchieveRx, The Quit Company, and Will Trade Under the Ticker QUIT


November 09, 2026 8:00am EST


### New name and ticker reflect a mission-driven company with one purpose: developing medicine for people who want to quit smoking or vaping. If approved, cytisinicline would be the first new medicine approved by the FDA for quitting smoking in 20 years, and potentially the first ever for quitting vaping.


SEATTLE and VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Achieve Life Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: ACHV) today announced that it has rebranded and will now be doing business as AchieveRx™, The Quit Company™ (AchieveRx or the Company), a late-stage pharmaceutical company focused on nicotine dependence. The Company’s common stock is expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under the new ticker symbol QUIT on November 10, 2026. The Company’s CUSIP number will not change, and no action is required by shareholders. The Company’s website is now[www.AchieveRx.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=XAtx5BceJLJA3ZAxNpaINz20ttn-6KbbhYhTHICrEw_5Hl1lMgec1ohcCcHqaoi2rylCD0RzWySsmBol5Iz_4XHFoyuPnm8Pgpz7fPOFKZM=) .


AchieveRx has one mission: developing medicine for quitting both smoking and vaping. That medicine is cytisinicline, an investigational compound. Smoking is the leading preventable cause of death in the United States, and no medicine has ever been approved for quitting vaping. The change comes as a new leadership team moves the Company from clinical development toward commercial readiness.


**Chemistry, not character**


Nicotine dependence lives in receptors and chemistry, not in character. It deserves medicine backed by evidence and studied with rigor. That is what the new name stands for. Every act of quitting, at any age, any stage of life, and for any reason, is worth celebrating. Most adults who smoke want to quit, and about half try each year.¹ AchieveRx is developing cytisinicline for the next attempt. Three ideas guide the Company: Simplicity. Science. Second chances, for good.™


“Smoking is the leading preventable cause of death in the United States, and helping people quit is one of the clearest ways to improve human health at scale. As a critical care and emergency medicine physician, I’ve seen what smoking steals from families, and I’ve seen what returns in the moments soon after someone quits and in the years that follow. No new medicine for quitting smoking has been approved by the FDA in 20 years. Our new name and ticker say exactly what we are here to do,” said Andrew D. Goldberg, MD, Chief Executive Officer of AchieveRx.


**What smoking takes, and why every quit matters**


Approximately 25 million adults in the United States smoke cigarettes,² and nearly 18 million use e-cigarettes.² Smoking and secondhand smoke together cause more than 480,000 deaths in the United States each year.³ Secondhand smoke alone accounts for more than 41,000 of those deaths among adults who do not smoke and about 400 deaths from sudden infant death syndrome,³ and it causes respiratory infections, ear infections, and asthma attacks in children.³ Cigarette smoking cost the United States more than $600 billion in 2018, the most recent CDC estimate.⁴ Worldwide, tobacco use kills more than 7 million people a year.⁵ Behind each number are children, partners, parents, and friends who carry that loss.


**Studied in the US, in the people who smoke today, and for whom quitting is hardest**


Cytisinicline has been studied in three Phase 3 trials in people who smoke: ORCA-2 and ORCA-3, randomized, placebo-controlled trials published in JAMA⁶ and JAMA Internal Medicine,⁷ which together enrolled 1,602 adults, and ORCA-OL, a 52-week open-label safety study. Separately, a Phase 2 trial, ORCA-V1, published in JAMA Internal Medicine, enrolled 160 adults who vape.⁸ Every ORCA trial has been conducted in the United States, and ORCA-2 and ORCA-3 enrolled difficult-to-treat patients by design: a mean age of 52 with no upper age limit (ranging up to 84), a mean of 36 years of smoking, and conditions including hypertension, COPD, type 2 diabetes, depression, anxiety, and a history of heart disease or cancer. Many had already tried to quit with medicine: approximately 42 percent of participants had used varenicline and 20 percent had used bupropion and were still smoking, and participants had made multiple prior quit attempts; those who smoked in ORCA-OL had made an estimated median of five quit attempts prior to enrollment.9[Read more in our recent release.](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=zC6rs5mUd2bKGcHcAXubs8kBpmxFieMunPiv2rCIjLRjFMkHdbedQNQPjlS98h9SWSQJhq-oZWeGRcoJVmdf_SyeToYb9nKgY1_Ikwoys5Y0_nVf7AkoBTyI9HGJQARLBzYd4tXU4t5C2QaLh5MonrzZmUbUBGRUf3H4_vGVqCGRyZ2ldfkWYPPC7_K3ndX2rV67Q8saupV7lvvyeac3BbI40BLdDP0adfhv26qkJqU=)


**About AchieveRx, The Quit Company**
AchieveRx, The Quit Company (Nasdaq: ACHV; QUIT effective November 10, 2026; formerly doing business as Achieve Life Sciences, Inc.) is a late-stage pharmaceutical company with a singular focus on nicotine dependence. AchieveRx’s mission is to develop medicine for people who want to quit smoking or vaping. That medicine is cytisinicline, an investigational compound. Three ideas guide the Company: simplicity, science, and second chances, for good™. To learn more, visit[www.AchieveRx.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=XAtx5BceJLJA3ZAxNpaINzEFhk0_4TIyCFUA2Mg47J7ClElSR-n5B5MCV7B-yZRibwkwGseggVH9yv4VYBYihrIiGKeeTgz9LYiJpE3xXRM=) .


**About Cytisinicline**
Cytisinicline is an investigational compound that binds to nicotinic receptors. It is being developed as an oral tablet to aid smoking and e-cigarette cessation in adults. The FDA has granted the vaping cessation program Breakthrough Therapy designation and a Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher. The New Drug Application (NDA) for cytisinicline for smoking cessation in adults is supported by two successfully completed Phase 3 studies (ORCA-2 and ORCA-3) and an open-label long-term safety study (ORCA-OL). The Company has also completed a Phase 2 study of cytisinicline in e-cigarette cessation (ORCA-V1) and held an end-of-Phase 2 meeting with the FDA.
